info.title: Artemis Studio API
info.description: Cluster-wide management and observability for Apache ActiveMQ Artemis

200.description: dryRun=true: connection probe result, nothing persisted
A stream of row, node, done, tail and failed frames.

resolvedReplyAddresses.description: What replyAddresses currently expands to, from the last scrape's addresses

replyAddressesCapped.description: The resolution cap cut the expansion short

VerifyRequest.description: Which indexed row to look for on the live broker.

VerifyView.description: Whether an indexed row is still on the broker.

presence.description: PRESENT, GONE or UNKNOWN. UNKNOWN is not GONE: a read that could not settle the question is never reported as an absence.

SqlQueryRequest.description: A query to plan or run.

NoticeView.description: Something true about a plan or result that changes how it should be read.

PlanView.description: What a query will do, worked out without contacting a broker.

source.description: BROKER or INDEX — which backend will answer.

targets.description: The queue-and-node pairs the query will read.

selector.description: The JMS selector the broker will evaluate, if any.

requiresScan.description: Whether any predicate forces messages to be read and examined.

pushedDown.description: The predicates the broker evaluates. These cost nothing.

scanned.description: The predicates Studio evaluates. These cost a scan.

estimatedMessagesExamined.description: How many messages the query is expected to examine.

effectiveLimit.description: The row limit that will actually apply, after the server cap.

notices.description: Everything true about this plan the operator has to be told.

IndexSubscriptionRequest.description: A request to start capturing a queue's messages into the index.

IndexSubscriptionView.description: One index subscription and what it currently holds.

messagesHeld.description: How many messages this subscription is currently holding.

bytesHeld.description: Approximate bytes of message payload held.

oldestObservedAt.description: The oldest observation still held, or null when nothing is held.

address.description: The address this queue binds to.

routingType.description: ANYCAST or MULTICAST. Cannot be changed once the queue exists.

durable.description: Whether the queue survives a broker restart.

filter.description: A JMS selector limiting what the queue accepts.

purgeOnNoConsumers.description: Delete the queue when its last consumer disconnects.

exclusive.description: Route to exactly one consumer at a time.

nonDestructive.description: Messages stay on the queue after delivery.

ringSize.description: Retain at most this many messages; -1 for unlimited.

autoCreateAddress.description: Create the address if it does not exist.

dryRun.description: Whether this was a preview that mutated nothing.

cap.description: The bulk safety cap in force.

overCap.description: Whether the summed estimate exceeds the cap.

partial.description: Whether some nodes applied the command and others did not.

totalAffected.description: Total messages destroyed, or that would be.

status.description: WOULD_APPLY on a preview; APPLIED when the node was changed; ALREADY when it was already in the requested state; SKIPPED_NOT_LIVE when the node was not live and never received the command; FAILED when it refused.

affected.description: Messages destroyed, or that would be destroyed, on this node.

subject.description: The id or address the close was aimed at.

routingTypes.description: Comma-separated routing types the address supports.

filter.description: A JMS selector limiting what the queue accepts.

BoundView.description: A limit the query ran into, which is why it stopped.

ResultView.description: A finished query, without its rows: those arrived as row frames.

nodes.description: Every target's outcome, including the ones that did not answer.

boundsReached.description: Empty when the query ran to completion.

partial.description: True when a bound was hit or a node did not answer.

RowView.description: A message, and where it came from.

nodeId.description: The node holding the message. Identity is (node, queue, messageId).

bodyTruncated.description: The management channel cut this body, so a body predicate may be a false negative.

source.description: BROKER or INDEX — an INDEX row may have been consumed since.

observedAt.description: When the index observed it. Null for a live broker row.

lastSeenAt.description: When the index last still saw it on its queue.

SqlNodeOutcomeView.description: What one node contributed, including nothing and why.

servedBy.description: JOLOKIA or CORE — the channel that served this node.

StreamFrameView.description: One frame on the query stream. The SSE event name says which field is set.

TailStatusView.description: What a live tail has seen, and what it can prove it missed.

enqueued.description: Messages enqueued on the tailed queues since the tail started.

everyMessageMatches.description: True when the query has no predicate, so enqueued minus shown is exactly the number that passed through unobserved. When false the difference also holds messages that simply did not match.

latencySource.description: How latencyMs was measured: OBSERVED (quantised to the sample interval, see latencyBoundMs) or MESSAGE_TIMESTAMPS (the messages' own clocks, normalised)

latencyBoundMs.description: The error bar on an OBSERVED latency, in milliseconds

requestEnqueuedAt.description: When the request says it was produced, on Studio's clock

requestSkewMs.description: How far into the future the request claimed to be produced. Forward skew only: an earlier timestamp is ordinary queue residency, not evidence of a wrong clock

verdict.description: UNKNOWN, IN_AGREEMENT, BROKER_SKEWED, or STUDIO_SUSPECT — the last meaning every node disagrees the same way, so the common factor is Studio's own host

skipped.description: Nodes not sampled this tick, each with the reason

rateExceedsInterval.description: The requested rate is faster than rr.sample-interval can deliver; the global interval is the floor

paused.description: True when the queue is paused on at least one node. A queue paused on some nodes and not others is a divergence the operator needs to see, so this is deliberately 'any', not 'all' — perNode says which.

NodeConfigEntryView.description: One configuration key on one node

NodeConfigSectionView.description: One section of a node's configuration

ConfigDiffView.description: Broker configuration compared across two nodes

ConfigEntryView.description: One configuration key, compared across both nodes

ConfigSideView.description: One node in a configuration comparison

DeletedView.description: How many captured messages the deletion destroyed.
